newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunis bourse index fell by 12 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Tunis bourse index fell by 12 pct in January.

text.p: The Tunis stock exchange index fell by 12 percent in January from the previous month, bourse statistics showed on Saturday.
The drop was higher than a 3.21 percent fall in December and a 0.9 percent decline in November.
Brokers linked the fall to the introduction of computerised dealing, with its greater transparency.

Since last October, the Tunis Stock Exchange has gradually introduced computerised dealing for listed companies, and the system now includes 25 out of 31 listed issues in the index. Most computerised shares dropped sharply when they made the switch.
The average index for January was 541.44 with the highest at 559.96 on January 3 and the lowest at 485.00 on January 31.
Average index in December was 588.21 with the highest at 598.11 on December 2 and the lowest at 570.64 on December 31.

Total volume traded in January was 48.84 million dinars, including 22.53 million dinars on the first market. In December, volume was 74.45 million dinars, including 33.76 million dinars on the primary market.

Average prices were down for most shares in January. Household firm AMS fell 48.55 percent, investment fund SPDIT-SICAF 44.82 percent, Industries Chimiques du Fluor 40.50 percent, and Banque de l'Habitat 40.1 percent.
Palm Beach Hotels dropped by 35.34 percent, chemical firm SPCD by 17.37 percent and beer and coke bottler SFBT by 16.22 percent after a 16.78 percent decline in December.

Chemical firm Al-Kimia, which fell an average 7.11 percent in December, rose 8.75 percent in January. Tunisie Leasing, which fell 33.25 percent in December, continued its downward trend in January by easing 5.81 percent.
Tunis Air rose 2.20 percent in January after a 20.26 percent fall in December. Retail stores Monoprix slid by 9.01 percent after a 11.6 percent drop in December.
The index closed at 492.45 on Friday.
